static_findings.result: BuildOptions defaults false. Transformation runs only in opt-in complete Linux executable build after existing LIR binding and ordinary CGU partition. Public emit/raw API paths are unchanged.

static_findings.area: exact function identity and reference closure
static_findings.result: Candidates come from nonforeign LIR FunctionId identities, not arbitrary symbol prefixes. All actual function/global initializer references are scanned; cross-unit references retain External. Duplicate definitions leave original preflight rejection intact.

Existing per-unit preflight, verified LIR equality, object-cache linkage identity and publication behavior remain in place. Forged LIR matches default rejection; missing entry, unsupported target and link failures preserve previous executable and sidecar.

Single-unit Clang closed path compiles transformed unit-0.ll while keeping reference sidecar unchanged; API and parallel Clang consume transformed units. Independently ran both backends and both unit configurations with FunctionRef and CallIndirect.

Opt-in may hide generated function identity symbols inside a complete executable. No claim that such symbols remain an external callable ABI. Main, runtime helpers, foreign declarations and noncandidate items retain prior linkage.

limits: Bounded backend contract review, not language-wide acceptance or a measured performance/runtime-quality gate. Actual function-address program passed native output/export checks in four configurations.
